title: Lemon Angel Food Cake
changes_from_base: Lemon zest and juice whisked into the meringue, less vanilla, berries to serve.
summary: This follows the classic angel food cake method, tin and bake, with lemon zest and juice whisked into the finished meringue and a little less vanilla. Light as air, fat-free in the sponge and served with fresh berries.
equipment: 25 cm two-piece tube (angel food) tin, ungreased and unlined
stand mixer or electric hand whisk
wire rack or glass bottle for cooling upside down

ingredients.item: cake flour (or plain flour; see note)
ingredients.note: plain flour works with a slightly firmer crumb

ingredients.item: large egg whites, at room temperature
fine sea salt or table salt, or table salt

steps.title: Heat oven, leave tin bare
steps.text: Position a shelf in the lower-middle of the oven and give it at least 20 minutes to reach 175°C (155°C fan). Do not grease the tube tin; the batter needs to grip the sides as it climbs, which is what lets it rise tall.

steps.title: Sift the flour
steps.text: Sift the flour with the first 150 g caster sugar three times. Repeated sifting aerates the mixture and makes it easier to fold into the meringue without knocking out air.

steps.title: Whisk the meringue
steps.text: In a spotless, grease-free bowl, whisk the egg whites on medium-low until frothy, then add the cream of tartar and salt and whisk on medium-high to soft peaks. Add the remaining 150 g sugar a spoonful at a time and whisk to glossy peaks that bend at the tip. Even a trace of fat or yolk stops whites foaming, so the clean bowl matters.

steps.title: Add the lemon
steps.text: Whisk in the lemon zest, juice and vanilla for a few seconds only. The cream of tartar keeps the foam stable despite the extra acid from the lemon.

steps.title: Fold in the flour
steps.text: Sift a quarter of the flour mixture over the meringue and fold it in with a few broad strokes of the spatula. Repeat until just combined, with no pockets of flour left. Gentle folding preserves the air bubbles that give the cake its height.

steps.title: Fill and bake
steps.text: Spoon the batter into the tin, run a knife through it to remove air pockets and smooth the top. Bake for 35-40 minutes until golden, the cracks look dry and a skewer comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool upside down
steps.text: Turn the tin upside down at once, resting it on its feet or over the neck of a glass bottle, and cool completely, about 2-3 hours. Hanging upside down stops the delicate sponge collapsing under its own weight while it sets.

steps.title: Release and slice
steps.text: Run a thin knife round the sides and the tube to release the cake. Slice with the serrated knife using a gentle sawing action and serve with the berries.

tips: A common mistake is greasing the tin; the batter then slides down the sides and the cake sinks, so always use a clean, ungreased tin.
Separate the eggs one at a time into a small bowl so a broken yolk does not spoil the whole batch of whites.
Add the lemon only after the meringue reaches glossy peaks, and whisk just long enough to combine.
Use a serrated knife; a straight blade squashes the airy crumb.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for up to 2 days. Wrapped slices freeze for up to 1 month; thaw at room temperature. Add the berries just before serving.
